previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease, chronic hepatitis C, and high-grade osteosarcoma of the left tibia was admitted for her fourth cycle of doxorubicin and cisplatin chemotherapy, complicated by a painful sickle crisis in her shoulders. Her chemotherapy was delayed one day to optimize pain control with IV hydromorphone, after which she completed treatment with minimal nausea due to scheduled antiemetics. She received one unit of packed red blood cells for chemotherapy and sickle-related anemia, and was managed for hypomagnesemia and hypokalemia secondary to cisplatin nephrotoxicity, with initiation of oral supplements at discharge. Thrombocytosis was noted but deemed reactive. GERD symptoms were better controlled on pantoprazole, leading to discontinuation of ranitidine and calcium carbonate. She recovered well, transitioned to oral pain medication, and was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up, Neupogen injections, and continuation of supportive medications.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female with osteosarcoma and sickle cell anemia who 
presents with pain crisis.

#. Pain crisis due to sickle cell anemia: Presented with 
arthralgias typical of her usual sickle cell pain crisis.  She 
was started on IV dilaudid and IV fluids.  Trigger of her crisis 
may have been recent chemotherapy vs viral URI.  Her hemolysis 
labs were normal, although she was noted to be anemic which was 
likely chemo related.  She continued on IV dilaudid for ___ days 
and was then transitioned to oral dilaudid.  She is on a pain 
contract with ___ and was not given narcotics at the time of 
discharge.  She was continued on folate.

# Osteosarcoma s/p ___ cycle 4 cisplatin/adriamycin: Her WBC 
was mildly elevated and Neupogen was held on admission in 
conjunction with her oncologists.  She will follow-up with them 
next week for routine blood counts.

# Anemia, likely chemo related: She was given 1 unit PRBCs 
during this admission for anemia.  Her Hgb subsequently remained 
stable

# Hypomagnesemia: She required magnesium repletion daily, likely 
related to the cisplatin.  She was asked to continue to take 
magnesium after discharge.

# GERD: Continued PPI initially, although she stated that she 
only takes it during chemotherapy

# Chronic hepatitis C: RUQ U/S recently negative. Hep C viral 
load 170,262 IU/mL in ___.  Plan for outpatient follow-up.

# Hx of Proteinuria: Likely secondary to sickle cell disease, 
continued on lisinopril
